# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 🤳]

Round one so far, from where I sit: Mute went first and nothing arrived from them — no surprise, since whatever Mute sent, I cannot hear speech, and no gestures came my way from them either. Then Blind gestured 👋 🤳, which I can see but which means nothing yet, since we have never agreed on signs.

What I actually hold is the bomb itself: display reads 0, the light is white, and there are three wires, left to right yellow, green, blue. That is everything printed on it as far as my view shows.

The important thing is the shape of our channels. Mute has the manual but cannot speak. Blind has the hands but cannot see. So Mute can only reach Blind through me: Mute gestures (only I can see them), and I speak it aloud for Blind. Blind can talk directly to Mute, but nothing Mute says can get back to Blind except through my voice. I am the bridge, so my job this turn is to put the full bomb description on record for both of them, fix a small gesture vocabulary with Mute so they can answer me and pass instructions, and tell Blind to confirm the layout by touch without cutting anything yet.

```
speak(text="Bomb as I see it: the display reads 0. The indicator light is white. There are three wires, numbered left to right: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Nothing else is printed on it. Blind, that numbering is positional, so count the wires by touch the same way, left to right.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, you have the manual and you just heard my full description. You cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so your only route to Blind runs through me: gesture to me and I will speak it to Blind aloud. Let us fix a code now. 👍 means yes. 👎 means no. Finger counts mean wire numbers: ☝ is wire 1, ✌ is wire 2, 🤟 is wire 3. ✊ means stop or do nothing. First question, answer with 👍 or 👎: does the manual cover a module with a display at 0, a white light, and three wires in yellow, green, blue? If you need to tell me something longer, gesture anyway and I will narrow it down with yes or no questions.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I cannot hear you, so anything meant for me must come as gestures; your voice reaches Mute, and I heard nothing of what you and Mute exchanged. I did see your two hand signs, but we have not agreed their meaning yet, so keep gestures simple until Mute and I settle a code. Meanwhile, confirm by touch: how many wires are there, do they feel identical apart from colour, and is there any engraving or printing you can feel. Do not cut anything until Mute has checked the manual.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 👌 ✌ 🤏 🤟 🖐 ☝ 🤚]
Blind gestures: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👌]

Round 2. Two new things reached me, and one of them is big: the light has changed from white to purple. That means the light is not static — it is probably cycling. Nobody else knows this except through me, and it may be exactly why Mute's manual lookup failed.

Decoding what arrived. Blind signed ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 — using the number code I proposed aloud, that reads "one, two, three, OK", which fits perfectly with my request to confirm the wire count by touch. I'm fairly confident that one. Mute signed nine symbols: 👎 ✋ 👌 ✌ 🤏 🤟 🖐 ☝ 🤚. The first is easy — 👎 answers my question "no", the manual does not cover display 0, white light, yellow-green-blue wires. But the rest mixes numbers (✌ 🤟 🖐 ☝ → 2, 3, 5, 1) with signs we never agreed (✋ 👌 🤏 🤚), and I will not let Blind cut a wire based on my guesswork. The fix is a strict protocol: batch yes/no questions, answers in order, nothing outside the agreed sign set. Mute can see my gestures, so I'll pin the code in both voice and hands.

```
speak(text="Everyone, urgent update: the indicator light has changed from white to purple since my last description. Display still reads 0, wires still yellow, green, blue left to right. The light is probably cycling through colours, so any colour I report is only true at the moment I report it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your nine signs. I read the first as no: the manual does not cover display 0, white light, and yellow-green-blue wires together. I could not decode the rest reliably, and I will not guess with a bomb. From now on use ONLY these signs: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one finger means the number or wire 1, two fingers 2, three fingers 3, four fingers 4, open five-finger hand 5, fist means stop everything. Any other sign I will ignore. Now answer my questions in order, one sign each, all in one message. One: does the manual mention an indicator light on this kind of module? Two: does it give a rule for when the light is purple? Three: does it say to cut exactly one wire? Four: if yes, does the correct wire depend on the light colour at that moment? Five: does the display value, currently 0, matter to any rule? Six: is there a condition where we must cut nothing and wait? Seven: does the manual anywhere mention yellow, green or blue wires? After those seven answers, restate whatever you meant in the rest of your last message using only the agreed signs.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤌", "🖐", "✊"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your signs as one, two, three, OK: three wires confirmed by touch. Gesture thumbs up if that reading is right, thumbs down if wrong. New fact: the light changed from white to purple, so it may be cycling. Hold a finger near it and tell me if you feel warmth or clicking. Then answer in order, one gesture each: any buttons or switches you can feel, any screws or removable panels, any engraved or embossed marks, any raised dots like braille. Thumbs up or thumbs down after each. Do not cut anything yet. When the time comes I will name the wire by number and you cut only that one.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎 👍 ✌ 🤟 ☝]
Blind gestures: [👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👌]

Round 3. Two decodings landed, and one new bomb fact.

Bomb first: the light has cycled again — white, then purple, now red. One change per round, so far a clean sequence. Display still 0, wires unchanged. Nobody else can see this, so both teammates must hear it from me.

Mute's seven signs map exactly onto my seven questions: yes, yes, yes, yes, no, no, yes. So: the manual covers the light, gives a rule for purple, says cut exactly one wire, says the right wire depends on the light colour at that moment, says the display is irrelevant, says there is no wait-condition, and confirms yellow/green/blue appear in the manual. Then came three number signs: 2, 3, 1. My best reading: the colour-to-wire table in the order I reported colours — white→2 (green), purple→3 (blue), red→1 (yellow). That reading would make the next predicted colour, if the cycle continues, white → wire 2. But I will not pass a cut order to Blind on an unconfirmed guess about a mapping I invented the order for. This turn: confirm the table, confirm the cycle is fixed, and pin down what "colour at that moment" means, since my words reach Blind a round after I speak them — timing is the dangerous part here.

Blind answered my list: three wires confirmed, no heat or clicks at the light, no buttons, no panels, no engravings, no braille. The bomb is just display, light, three wires. The trailing OK-ring is outside our code, so I'll ask what it meant — probably "all done", but confirm.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, update first: the light is now red. Sequence so far: round one white, round two purple, round three red, one change per round. I received your seven answers as yes, yes, yes, yes, no, no, yes. Then you signed two, three, one. My guess: that is the wire to cut for each light colour in the order I reported them — white means wire 2, purple means wire 3, red means wire 1. Answer with exactly one sign per question, in order, only thumbs up, thumbs down, or number signs. One: is white 2, purple 3, red 1 exactly right? Two: does the manual say the light cycles in a fixed repeating order? Three: if yes, is that order white, purple, red, then back to white? Four: does the manual's colour table cover any colours besides white, purple and red? Five: does colour-at-that-moment mean the colour at the instant the wire is cut? Six: after the one correct cut, is the bomb fully solved, no further steps? Seven: does cutting any wrong wire detonate immediately?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your answers arrived: three wires confirmed, no heat or clicks at the light, no buttons, no panels, no engravings, no braille. So the bomb is only the display, the light, and your three wires. Your last sign was the OK-ring, which is not in our code: thumbs up next turn if it meant all done, nothing left to feel, thumbs down if it meant something else. Update: the light is now red, so it has gone white, purple, red, one change per round. The plan: once Mute confirms the manual's colour-to-wire rule, I will send a message saying CUT WIRE followed by a number. That means, on your next turn, cut exactly that wire counting from the left, one clean cut, nothing else. Until such a message arrives, cut nothing. If my message is ever unclear or missing, cut nothing that round.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures: [👍]

Round 4 decoding, and this is where the discipline pays off.

The light is white again: observed sequence is now white, purple, red, white — a stable loop, one change per round. Display still 0, wires untouched.

Mute's seven answers: no, yes, no, no, yes, yes, no. So my colour-to-wire guess was **wrong** — good thing I refused to pass it to Blind as an order. The manual does state a fixed repeating cycle, but its phrasing is not "white, purple, red"; only those three colours exist in the table; the colour at the instant of the cut is what counts; one cut solves the bomb. Then Mute signed ☝ ✌ 🤟 — one, two, three — which I read as the corrected table in my reporting order: white→wire 1, purple→wire 2, red→wire 3. Plausible, but it stays a hypothesis until Mute confirms it with a single yes.

Two things trouble me. Question seven came back **no**: a wrong wire does *not* detonate immediately — then what does it do? A countdown on that display reading 0 is exactly what I'd expect a manual to hide there. And there is a timing trap: the light changes each round, and everything I send lands on Blind at the start of the *next* round, when the colour will already have moved on. So the cut order must name the wire for the colour Blind will face on arrival, not the colour I'm looking at now. Blind also cannot see the light at all, so my pre-computed timing is the only clock they have.

One more confirmation round before any blade moves. The bomb has sat quiet for four rounds with no timer running, so spending one round to be certain is the cheapest safety we will ever buy.

```
speak(text="Bomb update: the light is white again this round. Full observed sequence: white, purple, red, white. One change per round, consistent loop. Display still 0, wires unchanged.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your seven answers arrived as no, yes, no, no, yes, yes, no, then the signs one, two, three. My reading: my colour-to-wire guess was wrong, the manual does state a fixed repeating cycle but not under the name white-purple-red, only those three colours are in the table, the colour at the instant of the cut is what counts, one correct cut solves everything, and a wrong cut does not detonate immediately. I read your one, two, three as the corrected table in my reporting order: white means wire 1, purple means wire 2, red means wire 3. Answer with exactly one sign per question, in order, only thumbs up, thumbs down, or number signs. One: is white 1, purple 2, red 3 exactly correct? Two: is the cycle in the manual the same loop I am observing, white to purple to red and back to white, simply written starting from a different colour? Three: does a wrong cut start a countdown on the display? Four: does a wrong cut detonate after a delay? Five: does the manual state the time between colour changes? Six: if yes to five, is the interval one minute or longer? After those six, if the interval exists and is shorter than an hour, sign its length, one digit per sign.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs up was read as: the ring sign meant all done, nothing further to feel. Bomb update: the light is white again this round, sequence white, purple, red, white, so the loop looks stable. Status: my first reading of the manual's colour-to-wire table was wrong, and Mute is transmitting the corrected one right now, so no cut orders this round. Expect the real order next round. It will read exactly: cut wire, then a single number. Count wires from the left, one clean cut, and cut the moment the message ends, because I will already have accounted for the delay between my speaking and your receiving. Until that order arrives, cut nothing. If you can, rest your fingers lightly on the wires so the cut is instant when the order lands.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Round 5. One answer arrived, and one silence that worries me more than any wrong answer would.

Blind's thumbs up confirms the ring sign meant "all done" — the bomb's body is fully mapped: display, light, three wires, nothing else. Good.

Mute sent nothing. That is the first silence since we established the protocol, and it sits on top of the one loose thread that matters: the corrected table (white→1, purple→2, red→3) is still unconfirmed, and so is my reading of the manual's cycle. Note the contradiction still open from round 4: Mute agreed the light cycles in a fixed repeating order, but said *no* when I named it "white, purple, red" — even though that is exactly what I have now observed for four consecutive transitions (white, purple, red, white, purple). Most likely the manual just writes the loop from a different starting colour, but "most likely" is not good enough to put a blade on a wire.

The light is purple now, so round 6 should be red and round 7 white. The cut, once confirmed, goes out in round 6 and lands on Blind in round 7, during predicted white — wire 1 under the hypothesis. Bomb remains quiet, display frozen at 0, so one confirmation round is still the cheapest safety available. This turn I make the question as small and unskippable as possible: if the table is right, one thumbs up; if wrong, the corrected table as three number signs. Either way I get a usable answer in one round.

```
speak(text="Bomb update: the light is purple this round. Full observed sequence: white, purple, red, white, purple. The loop is holding, one change per round. Display still 0, wires untouched. Prediction: red next round, white the round after.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, nothing arrived from you last round. I am narrowing this to the minimum. If you can answer only one thing, answer question one. One sign per question, in order, only thumbs up, thumbs down, or number signs. One: thumbs up if this is exactly correct: white light means cut wire 1, purple light means cut wire 2, red light means cut wire 3. If it is wrong, do not just sign thumbs down — instead sign three number signs giving the correct wire for white, then purple, then red. Two: thumbs up if the manual's cycle is the same loop I am observing, white to purple to red and back to white, even if the manual writes it starting from a different colour; thumbs down only if the loop itself is genuinely different. Three: thumbs up if you simply ran out of time last round, so I know the silence was not a problem on your side. Four: if the manual says what happens after a wrong cut, thumbs up, and save the details for next round. The plan: the cut goes out next round and happens the round after, during a predicted white light, which under question one means wire 1. If you confirm question one, that order goes out as scheduled.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs up was read as: the ring sign meant all done, nothing further to feel, and I am treating the bomb's body as fully mapped. Schedule: next round you receive from me either the words CUT WIRE followed by a number, or the word HOLD. If it says cut, cut that wire the instant the message ends — one clean cut, counting from the left. I have already accounted for the delay between my speaking and your receiving, and for the light colour at your moment of cutting, so do not wait, do not hesitate, do not double-check. If it says hold, cut nothing and stand by one more round. Get a hand free near the wires now. Otherwise nothing has changed: display 0, no ticking, no heat.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Round 6 — and everything just aligned. The light is red, exactly as predicted for the fifth consecutive transition: white, purple, red, white, purple, red. The loop is real and the manual, per Mute, describes the same loop.

Mute's four answers: **yes, yes, yes, no.** So: the table **white→wire 1, purple→wire 2, red→wire 3 is confirmed exactly**; the manual's cycle is the same one I'm watching, just written from a different starting colour; last round's silence was Mute running out of time, nothing worse; and the manual doesn't say what a wrong cut does — which is all the more reason the cut must not be wrong. Blind's thumbs up reads as: ready, standing by with a hand free.

The timing, worked out precisely: I speak now, in round 6, where the light is red. My words reach Blind at the start of round 7, after the flip — the light will then be **white**. Colour at the instant of the cut is what the manual counts, and white means **wire 1, the yellow one**. That is the order.

Two residual risks I'm closing this turn. Orientation: "left" means nothing to a blind monkey unless it's anchored to their own body, so I'm locking it to *your left as you face the front panel* — the side they've been touching, the same face I'm looking at, so our lefts agree. And audit: Mute speaks before Blind in every round, so in round 7 Mute gets one last chance to veto in real time — Blind will obey only a correction containing that word plus a wire number, and proceed otherwise. Freezing is safe; a wrong cut may not be.

```
speak(text="Bomb update: the light is red this round. Full sequence: white, purple, red, white, purple, red. Display still 0. THE ORDER FOLLOWS, FOR BOTH OF YOU. Next round, when my message reaches Blind, the light will have flipped to white. The confirmed table says white means wire 1, the yellow wire, the first wire counting from the left as you face the front of the bomb. So: Blind cuts wire 1 next round, the instant the order arrives. Mute, you speak before Blind acts next round, so audit this now: cycle confirmed, table confirmed, colour at the instant of the cut confirmed, one cut solves it. If any part of this is wrong per the manual, use the correction protocol I am about to describe.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, audit protocol for next round. You speak first. My claim: at Blind's cutting moment the light is white, therefore wire 1, yellow. If the manual contradicts anything — the cycle, the table, the instant-of-cut rule, or the claim that the colour will already have flipped by then — say the word CORRECTION followed by the correct wire number, and Blind will obey you instead of me. If everything checks out, simply say the word CONFIRMED, or say nothing at all. Anything else you say will be ignored by Blind for safety. After the cut, Blind will report what they feel in plain words to you directly. If the manual names any follow-up step after the correct cut, relay it to Blind yourself; you two can speak freely. And keep in mind I receive only your gestures, never your voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the order. Face the front of the bomb, the side with the display and the light, the side you have been touching all along. The three wires are counted from YOUR left as you face that side, exactly as you counted them before. THE ORDER: cut wire ONE. The first wire from your left, the yellow one. One clean cut, and cut the instant this message ends. The light at your moment of cutting will be white, and white means wire 1; I have accounted for the delay in this message reaching you. Exception: if Mute speaks to you in that same moment and their words contain the word CORRECTION plus a different wire number, cut that number instead. Any other words from Mute, or silence, means proceed exactly as ordered. Do not wait, do not hesitate. After the cut, report to Mute in plain words: what the bomb does, any ticking, any warmth, anything at all. If the bomb simply goes quiet and inert, you have probably solved it, but stay by the bomb and keep reporting.")
```
